anchorData:
PHENOMENON FIGURES (approximate classroom values, use exactly): Eliud Kipchoge, marathon world record 2:01:09 at Berlin 2022 = 7,269 s over 42.195 km. Average pace = 7,269 / 42.195 = 172.3 s per km, about 2 min 52 s per km, about 20.9 km/h. Body mass about 52 kg. Energy cost of running is about 1 kcal per kg per km, so a marathon costs about 52 x 42.195 = 2,194, so about 2,200 kcal. Stored glycogen in muscle and liver is about 500 g = about 2,000 kcal (500 x 4).

TABLE 1. Nutrients per 100 g of prepared food (g carbohydrate / g protein / g fat = energy in kcal). Energy = 4 x C + 4 x P + 9 x F.
Ugali (cooked, stiff): 26 / 2.5 / 0.6 = 119.4 kcal (104 + 10 + 5.4)
Githeri (maize and beans, boiled, little oil): 18 / 6 / 1.0 = 105 kcal (72 + 24 + 9)
Boiled beans: 21 / 8 / 0.5 = 120.5 kcal (84 + 32 + 4.5)
Sukuma wiki (cooked with a little oil): 5 / 2.5 / 3 = 57 kcal (20 + 10 + 27)
Whole milk: 4.7 / 3.3 / 3.9 = 67.1 kcal (18.8 + 13.2 + 35.1)
Boiled egg: 1 / 13 / 11 = 155 kcal (4 + 52 + 99)
Dried omena: 0 / 60 / 8 = 312 kcal (240 + 72)
Roasted groundnuts: 16 / 26 / 49 = 609 kcal (64 + 104 + 441)
Mandazi: 45 / 6 / 15 = 339 kcal (180 + 24 + 135)
Nyama choma (grilled beef): 0 / 27 / 15 = 243 kcal (108 + 135)
Ripe banana: 23 / 1.1 / 0.3 = 99.1 kcal (92 + 4.4 + 2.7)
Boiled sweet potato: 20 / 1.6 / 0.1 = 87.3 kcal (80 + 6.4 + 0.9)
Sugarcane juice: 18 / 0 / 0 = 72 kcal
Dry maize flour: 73 / 8 / 3.5 = 355.5 kcal (292 + 32 + 31.5)

TABLE 2. Food test results (classroom concentration):
Maize flour: iodine blue-black (starch present); Benedict's stays blue (no reducing sugar); Biuret stays blue.
Sweet potato: iodine blue-black; Benedict's green-yellow (a little reducing sugar).
Ripe banana: iodine faint brown-orange (little starch left); Benedict's orange to brick-red (reducing sugar).
Sugarcane juice: Benedict's stays blue (sucrose is non-reducing); after boiling with dilute HCl, neutralising with sodium hydrogencarbonate and retesting, Benedict's gives brick-red.
Beans, milk, egg white, omena: Biuret violet (protein present). Ugali: Biuret stays blue (protein too little to detect).
Groundnuts, cooking oil, mandazi, nyama choma: brown paper test gives a translucent spot that stays after drying (lipid present); emulsion test gives a cloudy white layer for groundnuts and cooking oil. Maize flour: no translucent spot.

TABLE 3. Amylase investigation. 1% starch solution plus saliva amylase; time for iodine to stop turning blue-black. Relative rate = 60 / time in seconds (per min).
Temperature: 0 C: not cleared in 600 s, rate 0; 20 C: 300 s, rate 0.2; 37 C: 60 s, rate 1.0; 60 C: not cleared in 600 s, rate 0; 80 C: not cleared in 600 s, rate 0.
pH at 37 C: pH 2: not cleared in 600 s, rate 0; pH 4: 240 s, rate 0.25; pH 6.8: 60 s, rate 1.0; pH 9: 180 s, rate 0.33; pH 12: not cleared in 600 s, rate 0.
At 37 C the reaction is 5 times faster than at 20 C (1.0 / 0.2).

TABLE 4. Three athlete meals for Lesson 6.
Meal A: ugali 300 g + beans 150 g + sukuma wiki 100 g + milk 250 g. Carbs 126.25 g, protein 30.25 g, fat 15.3 g. Energy 763.7 kcal (505 + 121 + 137.7). Energy shares: carbohydrate 66%, protein 16%, fat 18%.
Meal B: githeri 400 g + sukuma wiki 100 g. Carbs 77 g, protein 26.5 g, fat 7 g. Energy 477 kcal (308 + 106 + 63). Shares: carbohydrate 65%, protein 22%, fat 13%.
Meal C: mandazi 200 g + nyama choma 100 g. Carbs 90 g, protein 39 g, fat 45 g. Energy 921 kcal (360 + 156 + 405). Shares: carbohydrate 39%, protein 17%, fat 44%.
Comparisons: energy C > A > B. Carbohydrate A > C > B. Protein C > A > B. Fat C > A > B. Fat share is highest in C (44%) and lowest in B (13%).
characters: Eliud Kipchoge: Kenyan marathon runner from Nandi County who trains near Iten, Rift Valley; 2:01:09 at Berlin 2022; about 52 kg. Iten, Rift Valley: high-altitude town known as the home of champions; athletes there eat mainly ugali, githeri, sukuma wiki, beans and milk. Learners: Grade 10 students, unnamed, working in groups of 4; a class DQB (Driving Question Board) and one class model on chart paper. Ugali: stiff maize-meal porridge, mainly starch. Githeri: boiled maize and beans. Omena: dried small lake fish from Lake Victoria (Kisumu market). Mama Wanjiru: a fictional canteen cook in Eldoret who prepares athlete meals; use her only for Lesson 6. Saliva amylase: enzyme in the mouth that breaks starch to maltose, which is why chewed ugali tastes sweet. Teachers may mention Mombasa, Kericho and Nairobi as other places, but must not add new figures.
outcome: A plate of ugali, beans, sukuma wiki and milk is not plain: it contains the chemicals of life. Carbohydrates (starch in maize) supply and store energy as glucose and glycogen, proteins (beans, milk, omena) supply amino acids for growth and repair and also make enzymes, and lipids (milk fat, groundnuts, cooking oil) store a lot of energy and insulate. Enzymes such as amylase work best at about 37 C and near neutral pH and break big food molecules into small ones the body can absorb, so these simple foods can fuel a 2-hour marathon. Evidence from Table 4 shows Meal A (ugali, beans, sukuma wiki and milk) best supports an endurance athlete because it gives the most carbohydrate (126.25 g), adequate protein (30.25 g) and moderate fat (18% of energy).
conventions: Use 'chemicals of life' for the three groups taught: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins. Lesson 1 may only name water, vitamins, minerals and nucleic acids as other chemicals, with no teaching. Enzymes are proteins and are taught in Lesson 5 only. Use g for mass, kcal for energy (not Calories, not kJ), per 100 g for Table 1 values, and Energy = 4 x C + 4 x P + 9 x F (Atwater factors 4, 4, 9 kcal per g). Say 'reducing sugar' (glucose, fructose, maltose; positive with Benedict's) versus 'non-reducing sugar' (sucrose). Sugar types: monosaccharide (glucose, fructose), disaccharide (sucrose, maltose), polysaccharide (starch, glycogen, cellulose). Say 'amino acids' for building blocks of protein and 'fatty acids and glycerol' for lipids. Colours: iodine blue-black = starch; Benedict's blue to green to orange to brick-red; Biuret blue to violet; brown paper translucent spot; emulsion cloudy white. Temperature in C. 'Optimum' means the temperature or pH with the fastest rate. Use 'denatured' for an enzyme whose shape is permanently changed by heat or extreme pH. Safety: Benedict's and HCl tests need goggles, hot water bath, no tasting lab samples. Name Kipchoge's record as 2:01:09 only. The DQB and the single cumulative model are updated in every lesson and finalised in Lesson 6. Do not call a meal 'best' without citing Table 4 numbers.

lessonMap.focus: A plain plate with extraordinary results
lessonMap.teaches: Launch of the phenomenon: ugali and beans are made of chemicals of life, and the three main groups are carbohydrates, lipids and proteins, named with a one-line role each (no structure, no tests)
lessonMap.buildsOn: No earlier lesson; learners use only prior knowledge from home and primary school
lessonMap.usesData: Kipchoge figures (7,269 s, 172.3 s per km, about 2,200 kcal, glycogen about 2,000 kcal) and Table 1 as a brief look; learners draw an initial model and start the DQB

lessonMap.focus: Carbohydrates: starch, sugars and how to test for them
lessonMap.teaches: Carbohydrate structure (mono-, di-, polysaccharides) and how to use iodine and Benedict's tests, including reducing versus non-reducing sugar
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: carbohydrates named as the energy chemical; maize in ugali; initial model
lessonMap.usesData: Table 2 rows for maize flour, sweet potato, ripe banana and sugarcane juice; Table 1 carbohydrate values for ugali, banana, sweet potato, sugarcane juice

lessonMap.focus: Proteins: building and repairing the body
lessonMap.teaches: Proteins are chains of amino acids; Biuret test; roles of proteins in growth and repair of muscle
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1 (protein named) and Lesson 2 (testing method and recording results in a table); adds protein to the model
lessonMap.usesData: Table 2 Biuret results for beans, milk, egg white, omena and ugali; Table 1 protein values for beans, milk, egg, omena, ugali

lessonMap.teaches: Lipids (fats, oils, waxes) are made of fatty acids and glycerol; emulsion and brown paper tests; roles in energy storage and insulation, with 9 kcal per g
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1 (lipids named); Lesson 2 and 3 (food tests); Lesson 2 energy values compared to Lesson 4 fat energy
lessonMap.usesData: Table 2 lipid results for groundnuts, cooking oil, mandazi, nyama choma; Table 1 fat values and energy for groundnuts, mandazi, nyama choma

lessonMap.focus: Enzymes: why chewed ugali tastes sweet
lessonMap.teaches: Enzymes are protein catalysts that break down food; effect of temperature and pH on rate; enzyme specificity and denaturation, with data interpretation
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2 (starch and Benedict's or iodine tests; maltose is a reducing sugar); Lesson 3 (enzymes are proteins made of amino acids)
lessonMap.usesData: Table 3 amylase temperature and pH data, including the relative rate calculation and the 5 times comparison

lessonMap.focus: Which meal best supports the athlete?
lessonMap.teaches: Using evidence to compare meals: calculate and compare nutrient and energy values, argue a claim with evidence and reasoning, and give the final explanation of the phenomenon
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1 to 5: all three chemicals, their tests and roles, Atwater energy values, and enzymes as digestion helpers; all DQB questions revisited
lessonMap.usesData: Table 4 (Meals A, B, C) with Table 1 and the Kipchoge energy figures (2,200 kcal marathon, 2,000 kcal glycogen); final model and answer to the DQB
